source: Sajid, Ball, Parr, Friston (2021) Active inference: demystified and compared
finding: Flattening the prior preferences in an active inference agent is the same as treating reward as just another observation. The agent is still told about reward but it does not drive value.
numbers: Setup: modified FrozenLake (Gym), 200 trials x 500 episodes, 5 agents.
quote: Flattening of the prior preferences ... is equivalent to reclassifying reward as just another state or observation
limits: Toy grid world. Authors say the equivalence is not exact: the change is in the agent, not the environment.
agent_relevance: Reward-free mode: keep a goal-free objective and the agent can still act. Treat reward as one observation channel.

source: Sajid, Ball, Parr, Friston (2021) Active inference: demystified and compared
finding: Stationary and stochastic FrozenLake scores. All goal-driven agents solve the stationary case. In the stochastic case only active inference stays near ceiling.
numbers: Deterministic / stochastic mean score [95% CI]: Q-learning eps decaying 97.79 [97.41,98.16] / 66.08 [63.28,68.88]; Q-learning variant 80.44 / 65.13; Bayesian RL 99.76 [99.45,100.00] / 64.39 [60.33,68.44]; active inference 99.88 [99.64,100.00] / 98.90 [98.00,99.79]; active inference null model 50.03 / 50.22. (Row order of the two Q-learning variants was garbled in the text extraction.)
limits: Tiny MDP, authors' own baselines, little tuning described. No independent replication found.
agent_relevance: Not general superiority over RL. Shows a Bayesian generative model handles noise well.

source: Sajid, Ball, Parr, Friston (2021) Active inference: demystified and compared
finding: Non-stationary goal location: active inference recovers after one episode. Q-learning and Bayesian RL need about 40 episodes. Bayesian RL adapts worse at each reversal because of pseudo-count build-up.
numbers: Goal moved at episodes 21, 121, 141, 251, 451 (500 episodes, 200 trials). Q-learning with eps=0.1 adapts fairly quickly, faster than Bayesian RL.
quote: the agent simply infers that a switch has happened, and acts accordingly
limits: The active inference model had a context factor that encodes the switch. The RL baselines had none, so the comparison favours the model with the right structure.
agent_relevance: Give the agent an explicit regime hypothesis and it beats relearning. Fits a scaffold that tracks which frame is active.

source: Sajid, Ball, Parr, Friston (2021) Active inference: demystified and compared
finding: Reward-free behaviour. With all rewards zero, Q-learning stalls (score 0, 15 moves, circular policy). Belief-based agents keep exploring (Bayesian RL 39.94, active inference 44.00).
numbers: Table 2, 100 episodes x 100 agents. Reward only on goal: Q 96.00, BRL 99.89, AI 99.47. Goal 100, hole -100, step -10: Q 95.56 (3.53 moves), BRL 99.77, AI 99.52.
limits: Bayesian RL exploration here comes from its model uncertainty, not a separate bonus. Q-learning did not update without reward.
agent_relevance: Open mode: a scheme with uncertainty over the world model keeps exploring when no reward arrives. A pure value learner does not.

source: Sajid, Ball, Parr, Friston (2021) Active inference: demystified and compared
finding: Pure exploration: with preferences removed and likelihood learning on, the agent covers unvisited cells with no revisits and keeps making new non-overlapping paths. If it learns preferences instead, it can come to prefer holes just because it fell in them first.
numbers: 15 runs for likelihood learning, 10 runs for preference learning. Null model with no learning ended at the goal 44.0% of the time.
quote: I am the sort of creature that enjoys spending time in holes
limits: Qualitative figures only. Preference learning can lock in bad habits.
agent_relevance: Warning for open mode: learned preferences follow what the agent already does. Keep an outside check.

source: Tschantz, Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2020) Reinforcement learning through active inference
finding: FEEF objective with a learned model reaches optimal Mountain Car performance in a single trial. Reward-only and variance-bonus agents mostly fail to explore.
numbers: Sparse-reward Mountain Car, 25 episodes of at most 200 steps, 5 seeds. FEEF visited nearly all state space in 20 episodes; reward agent stayed in a region reachable by random actions.
limits: Workshop paper, 5 seeds, no statistical tests. Baselines are the authors' own ablations.
agent_relevance: Directed information seeking matters when reward is sparse.

source: Tschantz, Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2020) Reinforcement learning through active inference
finding: Boundary condition: on Cup Catch (sparse but easy to reach by chance) all agents converge in about 20 episodes, so directed exploration gives no benefit. On Half Cheetah run and flip FEEF beat SAC after 100 episodes.
numbers: Cup Catch, 5 seeds. SAC given as one fixed reference (max after 100 episodes), not step-matched.
quote: it is simple enough to reach the goal with random actions
limits: Model-based versus model-free comparison mixes model use and objective.
agent_relevance: Epistemic terms pay off only when random search fails. Switch them on conditionally.

source: Tschantz, Millidge, Seth, Buckley (2020) Reinforcement learning through active inference
finding: Reward-free Ant Maze: FEEF agent covers more of the maze than a random policy after 35 episodes.
numbers: 4 seeds; metric is percent of maze covered. Exact percent only in a figure.
limits: Baseline is random actions only. No count-based or curiosity baseline.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that EFE-style exploration beats random. Needs comparison to other intrinsic-motivation methods.

source: Tschantz, Baltieri, Seth, Buckley (2019) Scaling active inference
finding: Model-based active inference agent with reward as a Gaussian observation. About 10x better sample efficiency than DDPG on inverted pendulum and hopper; more state coverage on continuous Mountain Car.
numbers: Active inference stopped at 100 epochs on convergence; DDPG shown over 1500 epochs; 5 seeds.
limits: Exploitation runs used extrinsic value only (epistemic term off), so the gain comes from model-based RL, not from the free-energy objective.
agent_relevance: Sample-efficiency gain comes from the world model. Not evidence for the free-energy objective.

source: Millidge (2019) Deep active inference as variational policy gradients
finding: On CartPole-v1 the deep active inference agent reached mean reward 500, beating actor-critic and Q-learning in the final mean. Most of the gain came from the entropy term, not the epistemic term.
numbers: 20 trials x 15000 episodes per agent. Without the entropy term the agent converged lower, similar to actor-critic and slightly better than Q-learning.
quote: We found little to no difference when the epistemic value was not computed
limits: Mean hides a bimodal outcome: runs reach 500 or collapse near 0 (policy collapse), so the mean counts successful runs.
agent_relevance: Entropy regularisation (keep options open) did the work. The information term did not.

source: Millidge (2019) Deep active inference as variational policy gradients
finding: Epistemic value had no measurable effect on CartPole, Acrobot or Lunar Lander. Author's reasons: easy tasks, noisy bootstrapped value estimates, and the epistemic term shrinking far below the extrinsic reward as the model improves.
numbers: Lunar Lander: active inference underperformed direct policy gradients, was comparable to other baselines. Author blames inaccurate EFE value network.
limits: Single-author preprint, small control tasks. Lack of effect may be task-dependent.
agent_relevance: Epistemic bonuses fade as the model is learned. Expect little effect on easy tasks.

source: Millidge, Tschantz, Buckley (2021) Whence the expected free energy?
finding: EFE is not just free energy applied to the future. The natural extension (FEF) discourages information seeking. The FEEF objective, a divergence between predicted and desired futures, has the epistemic term and equals VFE with a biased model.
numbers: Theory paper, no benchmark. EFE and FEF differ in the sign of the information gain term.
quote: exploration does not directly follow from free energy minimization into the future
limits: Depends on a temporal mean-field assumption and discrete time. Authors note the continuous-time version may differ.
agent_relevance: Exploration drive is a design choice added to the objective, not a free consequence.

source: Da Costa, Sajid, Parr, Friston, Smith (2023) Reward maximisation through discrete active inference
finding: Proof: standard active inference gives Bellman-optimal actions only for planning horizon 1 on POMDPs. Sophisticated inference gives Bellman-optimal actions on any finite horizon (recovers backward induction as temperature goes to zero).
numbers: Holds for finite-horizon POMDPs with known transitions and exact state estimation.
limits: Needs exact inference and a known model. Sophisticated scheme does not generally do exact inference, so optimality is not guaranteed in practice.
agent_relevance: Planning deeper than one step needs recursive evaluation, not one-step EFE.

source: Wei (2024) Value of information and reward specification in active inference and POMDPs
finding: EFE policy approximates the Bayes-optimal RL policy via information value. Regret gap is linear in horizon and quadratic in information gain. EFE improves on an open-loop policy by a term linear in information gain.
numbers: Theorem 5.5: bounds under a density-ratio bound C and belief-MDP assumptions. Reward and information gain must be balanced by a temperature parameter.
limits: Author calls bounds conservative. Theory only.
agent_relevance: Epistemic value stands in for the value of information. Set the trade-off explicitly.

source: Fountas, Sajid, Mediano, Friston (2020) Deep active inference agents using Monte-Carlo methods
finding: MCTS-planned deep active inference agent in dynamic dSprites matched a reward-only agent on reward but explored more. In a second task it beat DQN and A2C and was comparable to PPO2 at 2M iterations, with less variance across runs.
numbers: Baselines at default settings from OpenAI baselines. Authors warn these are illustrations, not state-of-the-art claims. Full MCTS planner took about 4 days of training.
limits: Authors say it is not clear the full EFE gives performance benefits over simpler reward-seeking agents.
agent_relevance: Costly planning. Gains are variance and exploration, not return.

source: Champion, Grzes, Bonheme, Bowman (2024) Deconstructing deep active inference: a contrarian information gatherer
finding: Failed replication of deep active inference on dSprites. Only agents that maximise reward solve the task. The EFE-minimising agent picks almost one action every time and fails, whatever action-selection rule is used.
numbers: CHMM[reward] with eps-greedy beat the other models; with best-action selection it matched PPO with higher variance; softmax failed for all. A2C and DQN reached similar asymptote; PPO higher.
quote: the appropriate formulation of the epistemic value in deep active inference remains an open question
limits: Their implementation differs from Fountas et al. DAIMC, which does solve dSprites.
agent_relevance: Check that the information term really picks informative actions and not merely predictable ones.

source: Champion, Grzes, Bonheme, Bowman (2024) Deconstructing deep active inference: a contrarian information gatherer
finding: Adding even 1% of the information gain to the reward objective after 200K steps drastically cuts reward. Reward and EFE agents behave alike only when the reward coefficient is very large (1, 1000, 2000, 5000 tested).
numbers: Table 1 sweep over prior-preference precision. The reward agent got worse as precision grew until a deeper critic was added.
limits: Specific to the amortised KL-based epistemic term in deep models.
agent_relevance: Information weight is a fragile hyperparameter.

source: Champion, Grzes, Bonheme, Bowman (2024) Deconstructing deep active inference: a contrarian information gatherer
finding: Tabular test shows the deep epistemic value can go the wrong way: it rises when the prior moves closer to the posterior, so it favours focus on one outcome and does not promote exploration.
numbers: Two controlled tabular experiments (Figure 14).
quote: the epistemic value used in deep active inference can behave degenerately
limits: Flaw of one form of epistemic term, not of all information-gain objectives.
agent_relevance: Do not copy a KL-between-posterior-and-prior form blindly.

source: Mazzaglia, Verbelen, Dhoedt (2021) Contrastive active inference
finding: Contrastive active inference matches reward-based RL on image tasks and beats likelihood-based active inference, which failed to converge in all runs on Reacher.
numbers: DeepMind Control Reacher Easy/Hard, 1000-step trajectories. Contrastive methods about 16% faster than Dreamer; likelihood AIF 224% slower. On Distracting Reacher Easy, Dreamer failed while contrastive variants succeeded.
limits: Goal reaching, not reward-free. Few tasks.
agent_relevance: Pixel reconstruction wastes capacity on distractors. Keep representations task-relevant.

source: Hafner, Ortega, Ba, Parr, Friston, Heess (2022) Action and perception as divergence minimization
finding: Frames task reward, information gain, empowerment and skill discovery as cases of one divergence objective. Argues for unsupervised exploration with world models, making task rewards optional.
numbers: Abstract only seen. No benchmark numbers recorded.
limits: Not read beyond the abstract.
agent_relevance: Supports an open mode built on a world model.

source: Prakki (2025) Active inference for self-organizing multi-LLM systems
finding: An active inference controller picks prompts and search strategies for an LLM research agent. The paper shows learned observation matrices and a shift from information gathering to prompt testing. No baseline comparison.
numbers: 3 state factors, 7 observation modalities. No success rates, seeds or baseline reported.
limits: Qualitative only. Fixed prompt set; author lists a growing state space as future work.
agent_relevance: Proof of concept only. No evidence that EFE control beats a bandit or heuristic over prompts.

source: Wen (2025) A framework for inherently safer AGI through language-mediated active inference
finding: Proposes natural-language beliefs and preferences with active inference over LLM agents. The paper says it is conceptual and outlines ARC experiments for the future.
numbers: No measured results. Percentages in the text are example messages.
limits: No data.
agent_relevance: No empirical support yet for LLM active inference on ARC.

source: Active inference as context acquisition for AI agents (arXiv 2608.19202)
finding: Search snippet only: links the EFE decomposition to LLM question-asking as a design language.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers seen.
limits: Unverified.
agent_relevance: Check before use; may bear on asking questions in open mode.

source: Know you before you speak (arXiv 2605.24647)
finding: Search snippet only: applies an EFE objective with an exploration term to user-state modelling for LLM personalization in multi-turn chat.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers seen.
limits: Unverified.
agent_relevance: Possible measured result on information-seeking dialogue; needs reading.

source: APEX agent post (Google developer forum)
finding: Community post claiming an EFE-minimising agent beats ReAct. The results table in the snippet had headers but no numbers.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Informal, not peer reviewed, no figures seen.
agent_relevance: Treat as unsupported.

source: Synthesis across opened papers (not a new study)
finding: Clean wins for active inference over RL are in tiny discrete tasks with built-in structure (FrozenLake). In deep benchmarks the gain comes from the model or from entropy, and the epistemic term often has little or negative effect.
numbers: Sources: Sajid 2021; Millidge 2019; Champion 2024; Fountas 2020; Tschantz 2019 and 2020.
limits: Synthesis. Missing: an independent large replication, and reward-free tests against count-based or curiosity baselines.
agent_relevance: Use the ideas (reward as one observation, explicit information value, regime variable) but expect no free performance.
